Old:
I brought my cat here about two years ago. I wanted them to check her for parasitic bugs beyond fleas because I was concerned she could have more than that (I’d seen some lice looking bug in a soap dish trap I set out in my room). They checked her ears since she’d scratch them a lot but the vet refused to check her body for anything else (after I requested) saying that it’s unnecessary. Fast forward to today, and I’ve been covered in mysterious bites since I’ve been in contact with my cat. They are BITES. Not acne, not allergies. They itch. Now I have to go see a doctor to see if they can identify what mysterious parasite is biting me. Praying it’s not scabies (which btw you’ll find sources online that say you can’t get it from a cat and sources that say that you can). And based on everything I’ve been experiencing, these bites seem to prove like you can…

I should’ve gone to a second vet. Now whatever infestation I have has been growing for those 2 years. My confidence has been ruined, my mental health, my finances. All that could have been caught early had the vet bothered to do his job.

I’m never recommending this spot to anyone.

I am extremely disappointed and heartbroken after my experience with Palmetto Animal Clinic. Due to what I strongly believe was negligence, my dog passed away shortly after receiving care at this clinic.

I brought my dog in for treatment on his back leg with Dr. Oliver. During the visit, he received an injection of vitamins and had blood drawn. Shortly after, his condition declined rapidly and unexpectedly. He began showing severe and alarming symptoms, including vomiting, intense shaking, inability to walk with his back legs, and his tongue turning purple which is a critical sign of oxygen deprivation (Cyanosis).

After the treatment I immediately told the vet that something was wrong and that his symptoms were not normal. Despite this, there was no appropriate sense of urgency, no escalation of care, and no recommendation to monitor him further. We were allowed to leave the clinic while he was clearly in distress.

There was also no clear explanation provided, no proper warning about potential risks associated with the treatment, and no accountability when his condition deteriorated. Given that French Bulldogs are known to be high-risk patients due to breathing issues (Brachycephalic Airway Syndrome), I expected a higher level of caution, monitoring, and professional judgment.

As a pet owner, you trust veterinary professionals to recognize emergency signs and act immediately. A purple tongue and severe distress should have prompted urgent intervention, closer monitoring, or at minimum, a recommendation to remain under observation. Instead, it felt rushed, as if the priority was closing the clinic rather than ensuring my dog’s safety.

This experience has been devastating. I strongly urge other pet owners to ask detailed questions, seek second opinions, and be cautious when trusting this clinic with their animals. No one should have to go through a loss like this under these circumstances.

I've had to clean diarrhea up everywhere, all over my house and bed, I never felt more like a lollipop then when walking into this new vet. My cat was dead within 2 weeks of their "treatment" All they did was try to protect themselves legally rather than try to assist me and my pet. Well, my pet is dead, they wouldn't refund my money, and had the audacity to try to defend themselves with lies in their response.
To top all of this off, when I came to leave this review, I found a fraudulent review already posted by me? That I never made. Please see image attached. At the end of the day, I did not see any tests performed only charged me for, and I picked up my cat sicker then I assumed he was before bringing him in. Don't be distracted by the razzle dazzle, ask all your questions before being charged.

Hello Gabriela, 
It would have been nice for you to elaborate on your review as to the 1 star, but I will.  The reason for your 1 star review is that you got upset when you were asked for the prior records of your pet, Mia, allow me to explain.  We ask any new client for the pet’s medical records so that the doctor can be informed of any treatment or condition your pet is being treated for or has been treated, in other words, it’s for the benefit of your pet and yours as well.   This is standard practice for us and majority of other medical professionals.  Upon asking you for the records, you became very defensive and rude with the front desk and stated, “What if I don’t have them, you won’t see my pet” to which she answered, No that is not the case, we will still see you pet.   You then said;  “Just let me know because I will go somewhere else”  the front desk stated, “that is your prerogative if you choose to do so”  at no time did she say anything rude to you or took on your rude attitude.  You were then seen by the doctor who once again explained to you why the prior records were asked for.  So, help me understand why this has caused you to take the time to do a bad review?  I totally understand a bad review if our service did not meet your expectations or something was not done correctly but because we asked you for prior medical records of your pet????? I welcome you to call me directly and discuss.  Wishing a bless day! 
Martica – Practice Manager
